overall: The AG declined to review the claim that public comment was cut short, since the chair controls public comment, and found the council did not violate the Open Meeting Law when the president had the complainant removed after disruptive, threatening conduct.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged he was not allowed to speak for the full three-minute public comment period at the May 5 council meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because it is within the Chair’s discretion whether to allow public comment at all, as well as to establish parameters for public participation during a meeting, an allegation that Mr. Dupuis’ public comment was cut short would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law in any event.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged he was unlawfully removed from the May 5 council meeting during public comment, before finishing his remarks.
allegations.key_passage: Here, based on Mr. Dupuis’ disruptive and threatening behavior, we find that Council President Onyski acted within his discretion under the Open Meeting Law when he instructed Mr. Dupuis to cease his comments and sought to have Mr. Dupuis removed from the meeting when he did not comply.
